newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin, Kuchma to meet, Black Sea row rumbles on.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin, Kuchma to meet, Black Sea row rumbles on.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin and Ukraine's President Leonid Kuchma will hold a working meeting on Thursday, Yeltsin's press service said on Monday.
It gave no further details but the meeting is expected to take place at the Barvikha sanatorium near Moscow where Yeltsin is now resting ahead of planned heart surgery next month.

Relations between the two ex-Soviet republics have long been dogged by a dispute over control of the Black Sea Fleet, based in the port of Sevastopol, that has prevented them from signing a friendship treaty.
In comments bound to upset Kiev ahead of Thursday's meeting, powerful Moscow mayor Yuri Luzhkov said on Monday that Russia should not concede any ground over the status of Sevastopol.
"Sevastopol is Russian land, it always was and always will be Russian land," Luzhkov, a Yeltsin ally, told Russian naval veterans in Moscow.

Luzhkov, a possible future contender for the Russian presidency, said Sevastopol had never been part of the surrounding Crimean region that was granted to Ukraine by Soviet leader Nikita Khruschev in the 1950s.
Other Russian politicians, including sacked security chief Alexander Lebed, have used the Sevastopol issue to demonstrate their nationalist credentials.
Russia's state Duma lower house of parliament last week urged the Kremlin to halt the long process of splitting the Black Sea Fleet, a move immediately denounced by the Ukrainian parliament.
"If the division goes ahead, both the city (of Sevastopol) and the fleet will be lost to both sides," Luzhkov said on Monday.
